summary: Intermittent TTFB spikes and mid-request closes due to edge proxy coalescing small chunked responses
description: Issue summary: Multiple customers (first reported by Inkware Studios on a Dedicated pool) observe occasional long TTFB spikes (10–45s) followed by connection close or 502/504. This occurs primarily for streaming completions where the runtime emits many very small chunked frames (1–4 bytes per chunk) and no Content-Length. Impact: customer facing API calls fail ~3–7% of requests during peaks, causing degraded UX for streaming LLM completions and some automatic retries that increase cost. Environment: Dedicated capacity in us-east-1 behind our edge proxy + ALB stack. Occurs across model variants that stream output. Steps to reproduce: 1) Create a streaming completion request that produces many tiny tokens (e.g., deterministic tokenizer, low temperature, model configured to flush per token). 2) Send request from a client with good network connectivity to the customer's dedicated endpoint. 3) Observe TTFB in client and ALB/edge proxy logs. Actual behaviour: Edge proxy waits until an internal buffer threshold is hit (~16KB) before flushing to the ALB, causing long TTFB for low-throughput streams; ALB idle timeout (60s) sometimes closes the connection before any bytes reach the client. Expected behaviour: First token(s) should be forwarded to ALB immediately as chunked frames so TTFB remains low and streaming continues. Temporary workaround: Customer increased runtime flush frequency (manual batch-flush) and we bumped ALB idle timeout to 90s for the Dedicated pool as a mitigation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a model run configured to stream output token-by-token (e.g., low temperature, token-level flush).
2) Issue a streaming completion request to the dedicated endpoint from a stable client in us-east-1.
3) Monitor client TTFB and edge-proxy access logs (see sample logs below).
4) Repeat at low token throughput (1–5 tokens/sec) to see coalescing behaviour.
sample_logs: [edge-proxy] 2026-03-13T15:03:12Z INFO - upstream response chunk (3 bytes) buffered; current_buffer=3B; threshold=16KB
[edge-proxy] 2026-03-13T15:03:27Z INFO - upstream buffer flushed to ALB after idle; flush_size=12B; elapsed=15s
[alb] 2026-03-13T15:03:55Z WARN - connection closed by target due to idle timeout; target_response_time=43s
[serving-runtime] 2026-03-13T15:03:12Z DEBUG - stream token emitted; size=2B; flush_requested=true
investigation_notes: Initial triage: reproduced in staging with a synthetic low-throughput token stream. Client TTFB matched edge-proxy flush delays (tens of seconds).

Hypothesis: the edge proxy has response buffering/coalescing enabled for performance with small chunk suppression; it's waiting for a buffer threshold or idle window before forwarding to ALB. For very-low-throughput streaming workloads this behavior increases TTFB and risks hitting ALB idle timeouts.

Config review: proxy setting 'response_buffering' set to 'auto' which uses a 16KB coalescing threshold and a 15s idle flush. ALB set to default idle timeout of 60s. Dedicated pool had additional fronting proxies with legacy buffering rules.

Correlation: incidents spike when models emit many small tokens (deterministic outputs) and for customers on dedicated pools with extra proxy hop. No evidence of model runtime slowness; runtime is emitting quickly per logs.

Related issues: SUP-50122 (chunked requests causing timeouts) and SUP-91827 (stream silence due to header fragmentation) — similar class but different root cause (proxy coalescing rather than header bloat).
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-13: Customer reported ~5% failure rate on streaming completions over last 4 hours. Sent initial repro and asked for engineering triage.

Marco Valdez (SRE) 2026-03-13: Reproduced in staging. Edge proxy configuration causes coalescing. Raising to P1 due to customer impact. Temporarily increased ALB idle timeout for affected dedicated pool.

Rashmi Gupta (Serving) 2026-03-13: Serving runtime already emits flushes per token when configured. Suggest disabling proxy response coalescing for streaming endpoints or honouring chunk flush flag from runtime.

Marco Valdez (SRE) 2026-03-14: Applied edge-proxy config change in canary: response_buffering=disabled for /streaming/* route. Observed immediate TTFB improvement in canary (median drop from 18s to 120ms). Will roll to remaining hosts after smoke tests.
Inkware Support (Customer) 2026-03-14: Confirmed improvement on canary host. Requesting permanent fix and guidance for dedicated customers.
resolution_notes: Canary rollout of edge-proxy change (response_buffering=disabled for streaming routes) shows TTFB median reduced to ~120ms for low-throughput streams. Follow-up actions: 1) Roll change to all dedicated pool edge proxies (scheduled 2026-03-14 22:00 UTC). 2) Add traffic-based proxy rule: disable response coalescing when downstream uses chunked transfer or when 'x-streaming' header present. 3) Update Dedicated onboarding docs to recommend runtime-level flush settings and recommended ALB timeouts for streaming workloads. 4) Create infra task to add monitoring alerts for coalescing-induced TTFB >5s in streaming routes (INT-41207).
